topics.title: Counting long ago: tallies, Egyptian and Roman numerals

learn.hook: Long before anyone wrote the digit 7, a shepherd tied a knot in a rope or scratched a mark on a bone for every sheep that went out to graze.
points: The first counting was one-to-one matching: one pebble, knot or tally mark for each object.
Grouping makes counting faster. Tally marks are bundled in fives, so 3 bundles and 2 marks means 17.
Egyptian numerals used a picture for each power of ten: a stroke for 1, a heel bone for 10, a coiled rope for 100 and a lotus flower for 1000. You repeat the pictures and add.
Roman numerals use I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1000. A smaller symbol written before a bigger one is subtracted: IV = 4, XL = 40, XC = 90, CM = 900.
These systems have no place value and no zero, so big numbers need many symbols and sums like 347 × 26 become very hard.
learn.reallife: Clock towers, chapter numbers in old books and 'Class VIII' written on your notebook all use Roman numerals.

games.title: Ancient number facts
items: I before X is subtracted: IX = 10 − 1 = 9. Eleven is XI.
The Roman system has a symbol for zero.
Roman numerals have no zero at all.
In Egyptian numerals, changing the order of the symbols does not change the value.
Egyptian values are simply added, so order does not matter.
The Egyptian lotus flower stands for 1000.
Stroke = 1, heel bone = 10, coiled rope = 100, lotus = 1000.
The bigger symbol comes first, so add: C + L = 100 + 50 = 150.
XXXX is the standard Roman way to write 40.
Forty is written XL, which means 50 − 10.

quiz.q: What number is MCMXLVII?
quiz.explain: M = 1000, CM = 900, XL = 40 and VII = 7. Together that is 1947, the year India became independent.
quiz.mistake: Adds C and M (1100) instead of subtracting C from M

quiz.q: How is 49 written in Roman numerals?
quiz.explain: 49 = 40 + 9. Forty is XL and nine is IX, so 49 = XLIX.
quiz.mistake: Writes IL by subtracting 1 from 50 in one jump, which the standard rules do not allow

quiz.q: An Egyptian scribe draws 3 lotus flowers, 2 coiled ropes, 4 heel bones and 5 strokes. What number is this?
quiz.explain: Lotus = 1000, rope = 100, heel bone = 10, stroke = 1. So 3000 + 200 + 40 + 5 = 3245.
quiz.mistake: Just counts the pictures (14) or mixes up which picture means what

quiz.q: How many Egyptian symbols are needed to write 999?
quiz.explain: There is no place value, so 999 needs 9 coiled ropes, 9 heel bones and 9 strokes: 27 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Egyptian numerals use one symbol per digit like our system

quiz.q: Kabir's cricket scorecard shows three bundles of five tally marks and 3 single marks. How many runs is that?
quiz.explain: Each bundle is 5 runs, so 3 bundles = 15. Add the 3 single marks: 15 + 3 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1 mark instead of 5

quiz.q: Why is it hard to multiply big numbers using Roman numerals?
options: Roman numerals cannot show numbers above 1000
Roman numerals cannot show even numbers
There is no place value or zero, so digits cannot be lined up in columns
Letters are not allowed in maths
quiz.explain: Our column method works because each place has a fixed value. Roman numerals have no place value and no zero, so there are no columns to line up.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the problem is the size of numbers rather than the missing place value

quiz.q: Which of these Roman numerals has the largest value?
quiz.explain: DC = 500 + 100 = 600, CD = 500 − 100 = 400, CX = 110 and XC = 90. So DC is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a smaller symbol in front means subtract

quiz.q: Riya sees 'Chapter XIX' in an old storybook. Which chapter is it?
quiz.explain: X = 10 and IX = 9, so XIX = 10 + 9 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Adds every symbol (10 + 1 + 10 = 21) instead of subtracting the I before X

teach.ask: Gappu grumbles: Why does 888 need so many symbols in Roman numerals (DCCCLXXXVIII) but only three digits in our numbers?
teach.praise: Yes! Roman numerals only add and repeat symbols, but our digits get their value from their place, with zero holding empty places. Clever!
teach.nudge: In 888, do all three 8s mean the same thing? What gives each 8 a different value?

topics.title: Place value and the story of zero

learn.hook: With just ten symbols, 0 to 9, you can write any number you can imagine. The secret? Place value, and a humble little zero.
points: In a place value system, a digit's value depends on its position. In 555 the three 5s mean 500, 50 and 5.
Our system is base 10: each place is worth 10 times the place on its right (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands...).
Zero is a placeholder: 205 and 25 are different numbers because the 0 keeps the tens place empty.
About 4000 years ago the Babylonians used place value with base 60. The Maya of Central America used base 20 and drew a shell for zero.
Indian mathematicians built the base-10 system with zero as a number. Brahmagupta (7th century CE) wrote rules like a + 0 = a and a − a = 0. These numerals travelled through the Arab world to Europe.

example.q: Write 40,305 in expanded form using powers of 10.
steps: Zeros add nothing, but they keep the other digits in their places

learn.reallife: Every price tag, PIN code and cricket score uses place value. One extra zero turns a ₹500 note into ₹5000!

items.text: In 7,382 the value of the digit 3 is ___
Brahmagupta's rule: a number minus itself equals ___

quiz.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 4,60,213?
quiz.explain: Reading the places of 4,60,213 from the left: lakh, ten-thousand, thousand, hundred, ten, one. The 6 is in the ten-thousands place, so it is worth 60,000.
quiz.mistake: Reads the place of the digit wrongly because of the Indian commas

quiz.q: Which number is 3 × 10³ + 5 × 10 + 2?
quiz.explain: 3 × 1000 = 3000, 5 × 10 = 50 and 2 more. 3000 + 50 + 2 = 3052. The hundreds place is empty, so it gets a 0.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the zero in the empty hundreds place

quiz.q: Why does a place value system need a zero?
options: To show an empty place, like the tens place in 405
To make every number look bigger
To stand for the number ten
quiz.explain: Without 0, 405 and 45 would look the same. Zero holds an empty place so the other digits stay in the right positions.
quiz.mistake: Thinks zero is just 'nothing' and has no job to do

quiz.q: The Babylonians counted in base 60. A number shows 2 in the 'sixties' place and 5 in the ones place. What is it in our numbers?
quiz.explain: 2 sixties and 5 ones = 2 × 60 + 5 = 125. It is just like 2 minutes 5 seconds = 125 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits as if they were in base 10

quiz.q: Which Indian mathematician wrote rules for working with zero, such as a − a = 0, in the 7th century CE?
quiz.explain: Brahmagupta wrote rules for adding, subtracting and multiplying with zero in 628 CE, treating zero as a number.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Indian mathematicians with Greek ones

quiz.q: The Maya counted in base 20. A Maya number has 3 in the 'twenties' place and 4 in the ones place. What is it in our numbers?
quiz.explain: 3 twenties and 4 ones = 3 × 20 + 4 = 64.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits as base 10 and gets 34

quiz.q: We still use the Babylonian base 60 for time. How many seconds are there in 1 hour?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes and each minute has 60 seconds, so 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Adds 60 + 60 or multiplies by 10 instead of 60

quiz.q: Meena writes 'five thousand and seven' as 57. What did she forget?
options: Zeros to hold the empty hundreds and tens places
That place value works only for small numbers
quiz.explain: Five thousand and seven is 5007. The hundreds and tens places are empty, so they need zeros.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that empty places must be filled with zero

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: 205 and 25 use the same digits 2 and 5. Why are they different numbers?
teach.praise: I see! In 205 the 0 holds the tens place empty, so the 2 moves to the hundreds place. Place value is powerful!
teach.nudge: Where does the 2 sit in 205, and where does it sit in 25? What is the 0 doing?

learn.hook: Computers count with only two digits, 0 and 1. To a computer, 1010 means ten!
points: The base tells how many make one group before you move to the next place. Base 10 groups in tens, base 5 in fives and base 2 in twos.
In base 2 (binary) the place values are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ... So 1011 in base 2 = 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 11.
In base 5 the place values are 1, 5, 25, 125, ... and only the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 are used.
To write a number in base 2, break it into place values: 13 = 8 + 4 + 1, so 13 = 1101 in base 2.
Base 10 probably comes from our ten fingers, and base 60 still lives on in hours, minutes and seconds.
learn.reallife: Every photo, song and game on a phone is stored as long strings of 0s and 1s. That is binary, base 2.

quiz.q: What is 1101 (base 2) in our base 10?
quiz.explain: The places are 8, 4, 2, 1. 1101 means 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 13.
quiz.mistake: Just adds the digits (3) or reads it as a base-10 number

quiz.q: How is 6 written in base 2?
quiz.explain: 6 = 4 + 2. Places 4, 2, 1 get 1, 1, 0, so 6 = 110 in base 2.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the wrong order or uses the place values wrongly

quiz.q: Which digits are used in base 5?
quiz.explain: In base 5, as soon as you reach 5 you make a new group, so only 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 are needed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the base number itself is one of the digits

quiz.q: What is 32 (base 5) in base 10?
quiz.explain: 3 fives and 2 ones: 3 × 5 + 2 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Reads the number as base 10, or swaps the digits (2 × 5 + 3 = 13)

quiz.q: What are the first four place values in base 2, starting from the right?
quiz.explain: Each place is 2 times the one on its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ...
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 each time instead of multiplying by 2

quiz.q: Harpreet packs 19 laddoos in boxes of 5. How is 19 written in base 5?
quiz.explain: 19 = 3 boxes of 5 + 4 loose laddoos, so 19 = 34 in base 5. Check: 3 × 5 + 4 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Writes the remainder first, or uses the digit 9 which base 5 does not have

quiz.q: A movie lasts 150 minutes. How many hours and minutes is that?
quiz.explain: 150 = 2 × 60 + 30, so it is 2 hours and 30 minutes. Time works in base 60, not base 100.
quiz.mistake: Treats an hour as 100 minutes and reads 150 as 1 hour 50 minutes

quiz.q: What is the largest number (in base 10) that can be written using only 4 digits in base 2?
quiz.explain: The largest 4-digit binary number is 1111 = 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 15. The next number, 16, needs 5 digits (10000).
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2⁴ = 16 itself fits in 4 binary digits

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can a computer write the number 5 if it only knows 0 and 1?
teach.praise: Wow, 5 = 4 + 1, so in binary it is 101. Places go 1, 2, 4, 8! Computers are smart and so are you!
teach.nudge: What are the place values in base 2? Which of them add up to 5?
